title: Artin-Rees for coherent modules on a Noetherian scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, i.e. a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] whose underlying space is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. For a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal F$ and $t\ge1$ let $\mathcal I^t\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal M$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module](0) (the image of the multiplication map $\mathcal I^t\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$), $\mathcal I^0\mathcal M=\mathcal M$, and for two sub-$\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal M,\mathcal M'\subseteq\mathcal F$ let $\mathcal M\cap\mathcal M'$ be the sectionwise intersection, $(\mathcal M\cap\mathcal M')(W)=\mathcal M(W)\cap\mathcal M'(W)$. Then there is an integer $c\ge0$ such that $\mathcal I^{n-c}(\mathcal I^c\mathcal F\cap\mathcal G)=\mathcal I^n\mathcal F\cap\mathcal G$ for all $n\ge c$; in particular $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F\cap\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal I^{n-c}\mathcal G$ for all $n\ge c$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (a finite affine cover).* By [pqf-def-locnoeth], $X$ has an affine open cover $(U_i)$ with $R_i=\mathcal O_X(U_i)$ Noetherian; quasi-compactness of $X$ gives a finite subcover $U_1,\ldots,U_r$ (also when $X=\emptyset$, take $r=0$). Write $I_i=\mathcal I(U_i)$, $M_i=\mathcal F(U_i)$, and $N_i=\mathcal G(U_i)\subseteq M_i$. The quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal G$ of the coherent module $\mathcal F$ is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](2). Hence $M_i$ and $N_i$ are finitely generated $R_i$-modules by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a), and $I_i$ is an ideal of $R_i$. For every $t\ge0$, [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections](1),(2) identifies $(\mathcal I^t\mathcal F)(U_i)=I_i^tM_i$ and $\mathcal I^t$ as a quasi-coherent ideal (with $t=0$ by definition). Since the intersection is sectionwise, $(\mathcal I^t\mathcal F\cap\mathcal G)(U_i)=I_i^tM_i\cap N_i$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 01YA (lemma-Artin-Rees, line 2601): 'X has a finite covering by spectra of Noetherian rings'; the affine identifications use Schemes, Lemmas 01I8 and 01IC

proof.text: *Step 2 (one constant for the cover).* For each $i$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees] to $R_i,I_i,M_i,N_i$. Choose $c_i\ge0$ with $I_i^nM_i\cap N_i=I_i^{n-c_i}(I_i^{c_i}M_i\cap N_i)$ for $n\ge c_i$. Put $c=\max_i c_i$, with $c=0$ for the empty cover. This same $c$ works on every $U_i$: if $n\ge c$, first apply the equality for $c_i$ at $c$ to obtain $I_i^cM_i\cap N_i=I_i^{c-c_i}(I_i^{c_i}M_i\cap N_i)$, then multiply by $I_i^{n-c}$. The product of powers is $I_i^{n-c_i}$, so the result equals $I_i^nM_i\cap N_i$ by the equality for $c_i$ at $n$. This also covers $I_i=0$, $I_i=R_i$, $N_i=0$, and $c_i=0$.

proof.text: *Step 3 (the left-hand sheaf on the cover).* Put $\mathcal H=\mathcal I^c\mathcal F\cap\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F$. The inclusion $\mathcal I^c\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ is between quasi-coherent modules by Step 1. Its cokernel $\mathcal Q=\mathcal F/(\mathcal I^c\mathcal F)$ is quasi-coherent, and $\mathcal Q(U_i)=M_i/I_i^cM_i$, by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image](2),(3). The sectionwise kernel of the composite $\mathcal G\hookrightarrow\mathcal F\to\mathcal Q$ is exactly $\mathcal H$; it is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel]. Its sections on $U_i$ are $H_i=I_i^cM_i\cap N_i$, since an element of $N_i$ maps to zero in $M_i/I_i^cM_i$ exactly when it lies in $I_i^cM_i$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections](1),(2) applies to $\mathcal I^{n-c}$ and $\mathcal H$ and yields $(\mathcal I^{n-c}\mathcal H)(U_i)=I_i^{n-c}H_i$ for every $n\ge c$, including $n=c$ where the power is zero.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 01YA (lemma-Artin-Rees); the identification of the intersection with the quasi-coherent kernel expands its affine reduction using Schemes, Lemma 01IC (lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent)

proof.text: *Step 4 (equality of subsheaves).* By Steps 1 and 3, on every $U_i$ the two submodules of $\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ have sections $I_i^{n-c}(I_i^cM_i\cap N_i)$ and $I_i^nM_i\cap N_i$, respectively; Step 2 makes them equal for all $n\ge c$. Both are quasi-coherent submodules: the left by [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections](1) and Step 3, the right by the same kernel argument as Step 3 with $n$ replacing $c$. Their restrictions to $U_i$ remain quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2). On an affine scheme a quasi-coherent module is determined by its global-sections module [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3), compatibly with the two inclusions into $\mathcal F|_{U_i}$; hence the two subsheaves coincide on each $U_i$, and therefore on $X$. Finally $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal G$ implies $\mathcal I^{n-c}\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal I^{n-c}\mathcal G$ by the multiplication-image definition [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module](0), giving the stated inclusion after the equality.
